noun.title: Noun
noun.definition: A noun is a word that names a person, place, thing, or idea. It acts as the subject or object of a sentence.
noun.purpose: Nouns are the building blocks of communication, allowing us to identify what or who we are discussing.

examples.text: The talented teacher inspired the entire classroom.
examples.description: Refers to a specific individual or profession.

examples.text: We spent our winter holidays exploring Paris.
examples.description: A proper noun naming a specific geographical location.

examples.text: She couldn't find her brass keys anywhere.
examples.description: A concrete noun representing a tangible physical item.

examples.text: Honesty is valued above all other virtues.
examples.description: An abstract noun representing a quality, state, or concept.

examples.text: A proud flock of seagulls hovered over the dock.
examples.description: Represents a group or collection of individuals.

examples.text: The children played happily around the quiet neighborhood.
examples.description: A concrete noun representing a local area or district.

examples.text: Their shared laughter brought pure happiness to everyone.
examples.description: An abstract noun representing an emotional state.

examples.text: An international delegation of scientists visited the research lab.
examples.description: Represents a group of people delegated to act on behalf of others.

examples.text: The artist spent months finishing the marble sculpture.
examples.description: A concrete noun representing a physical artistic creation.

examples.text: A polite officer helped us find the correct train terminal.
examples.description: A common noun representing a person in a position of authority.

practice.question: Identify the abstract noun representing an idea in: 'Her boundless curiosity led to many discoveries.'
practice.explanation: 'Curiosity' is an abstract noun denoting a quality of mind, whereas 'discoveries' is a concrete/general noun, and 'boundless' is an adjective.

practice.question: Which word is a collective noun in: 'The lively jury finally reached a unanimous decision'?
practice.explanation: 'Jury' is a collective noun because it refers to a single body or group consisting of multiple individuals acting together.

practice.question: Fill in the blank with the correct proper noun: 'Last week, we went to visit Uncle _____.'
practice.explanation: 'David' is a proper noun naming a specific person, so it is capitalized and fits grammatically as a name.

practice.question: Find the noun in: 'The high-speed train flew past the quiet platform.'
practice.explanation: 'Platform' is a concrete noun representing a physical place/thing. 'Flew' is a verb, 'high-speed' is an adjective, and 'past' is a preposition here.

practice.question: Which of the following is an abstract noun denoting a state or emotion?
practice.explanation: 'Sorrow' is an abstract noun denoting a feeling of deep distress, which is an intangible state/emotion.

practice.question: Identify the noun in the sentence: 'The heavy rain caused minor flooding on our street.'
practice.explanation: 'Flooding' is a noun (gerund/process) denoting the state of being covered in water. 'Heavy' is an adjective, 'caused' is a verb, and 'on' is a preposition.

practice.question: Choose the proper noun in: 'Many tourists visit the majestic Grand Canyon every summer.'
practice.explanation: 'Grand Canyon' is a proper noun because it names a specific, unique geographical wonder and is capitalized.

practice.question: Which word is a collective noun? 'A large swarm of bees surrounded the sweet flowers.'
practice.explanation: 'Swarm' is a collective noun because it refers to a group or gathering of insects (bees) as a single unit.

practice.question: Find the concrete noun in: 'An amazing idea suddenly popped into his mind.'
practice.explanation: While 'idea' is abstract, 'mind' can be understood as the physical/mental faculty or container, but is considered a more concrete entity here compared to 'idea' or 'suddenly' (adverb) and 'amazing' (adjective).

practice.question: Select the noun that acts as the subject of the sentence: 'The friendly dog barked at the mail carrier.'
practice.explanation: 'dog' is the main noun performing the action 'barked', which makes it the grammatical subject of the sentence.

pronoun.title: Pronoun
pronoun.definition: A pronoun is a substitute word used instead of a noun or noun phrase to avoid repetitive language patterns.
pronoun.purpose: Pronouns make sentences flow more naturally by keeping us from repeating names and objects endlessly.

examples.text: He completed the assignment before the timer ran out.
examples.description: Replaces the male subject who performs the action.

examples.text: The manager called her into the office for feedback.
examples.description: Replaces the person receiving the action.

examples.text: That sparkling laptop on the desk is completely mine.
examples.description: Shows absolute ownership and stands alone without a noun.

examples.text: They cooked a gourmet four-course dinner themselves.
examples.description: Refers back to the plural subject 'They' to emphasize who did the action.

examples.text: These are the books that we ordered online last week.
examples.description: Points directly to specific plural items nearby.

examples.text: The musician who played the violin was exceptionally talented.
examples.description: Connects a subordinate clause to the main noun 'musician'.

examples.text: Can someone help me translate this English letter?
examples.description: Refers to an unspecified person in a general way.

examples.text: The two close friends always support each other.
examples.description: Expresses a mutual relationship or action between two subjects.

examples.text: The local guide showed us the most beautiful viewpoints.
examples.description: Replaces the group of speakers receiving the action as an indirect object.

examples.text: If this notebook is not mine, then it must be yours.
examples.description: Expresses ownership belonging to the listener without repeating the noun 'notebook'.

practice.question: Identify the reflexive pronoun in: 'The kittens washed themselves after eating dinner.'
practice.explanation: 'Themselves' is a reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject 'the kittens'.

practice.question: Choose the correct possessive pronoun: 'We own that car; the blue sedan is _____.'
practice.explanation: 'Ours' is a possessive pronoun that stands alone. 'Our' is a possessive adjective and requires a noun (e.g., 'our car').

practice.question: Which word is a demonstrative pronoun in: 'Those are the most delicious apples I have ever tasted.'
practice.explanation: 'Those' is a demonstrative pronoun pointing out specific plural objects at a distance.

practice.question: Fill in the blank: 'Alex and _____ are going to study English grammar together.'
practice.explanation: Since the pronoun is part of the subject phrase performing the action, the subject pronoun 'I' is correct ('Alex and I' is the subject).

practice.question: Identify the relative pronoun in: 'The book which you lent me was absolutely fascinating.'
practice.explanation: 'Which' is a relative pronoun linking the descriptive clause 'you lent me' back to the noun 'book'.

practice.question: Choose the correct indefinite pronoun: 'The room was completely empty; _____ had arrived yet.'
practice.explanation: The phrase 'completely empty' requires 'nobody' to logically make sense.

practice.question: Which word is a reciprocal pronoun in: 'The players congratulated one another after the fair game.'?
practice.explanation: 'One another' is a reciprocal pronoun showing mutual, shared action among the group of players.

practice.question: Select the subject pronoun in the sentence: 'Although they were tired, they completed the English quiz.'
practice.explanation: 'they' is a subject pronoun representing the group performing the actions 'were' and 'completed'.

practice.question: Fill in the blank with the correct object pronoun: 'Our teacher asked _____ to help clean the board.'
practice.explanation: Here, the pronoun functions as the object receiving the verb 'asked', which requires the object form 'us'.

practice.question: Identify the possessive pronoun that stands alone: 'My keys are in my pocket, but where are yours?'
practice.explanation: 'yours' is a possessive pronoun representing 'your keys' and standing alone without repeating 'keys'.

adverbs.title: Adverbs
adverbs.definition: An adverb is a word that describes, qualifies, or modifies a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. It tells how, when, where, why, or how much.
adverbs.purpose: Adverbs add precise details to actions, circumstances, and degrees, giving color and context to descriptions.

examples.text: She played the classical piano sonata beautifully.
examples.description: Explains *how* the action of playing was executed.

examples.text: We will leave for the global conference tomorrow.
examples.description: Details *when* the action will happen.

examples.text: Please put the shipping packages outside.
examples.description: Specifies *where* the objects should be placed.

examples.text: He always reviews his vocabulary cards before sleeping.
examples.description: Shows *how often* the habit occurs.

examples.text: It was an extremely challenging exams paper.
examples.description: Indicates the *intensity* or *degree* of the adjective 'challenging'.

examples.text: She quietly closed the heavy wooden door so as not to wake the sleeping baby.
examples.description: Describes the quiet and gentle manner in which the door was shut.

examples.text: They recently relocated to a stunning coastal town.
examples.description: Indicates that the move occurred in the near past.

examples.text: We searched everywhere for the lost set of brass keys.
examples.description: Denotes that the physical scope of search covered all places.

examples.text: He seldom watches television, preferring to read historic novels.
examples.description: Indicates a very low frequency of watching television.

examples.text: The English exam was quite straightforward, and everyone did well.
examples.description: Modifies the adjective 'straightforward' to indicate a moderate to high degree.

practice.question: Identify the adverb of degree in: 'The weather was incredibly hot during our desert safari.'
practice.explanation: 'Incredibly' is an adverb of degree modifying the adjective 'hot', showing how intense the heat was.

practice.question: Choose the correct adverb of frequency to fill the gap: 'She _____ forgets her keys, almost never!'
practice.explanation: The clue 'almost never' matches 'rarely', which means very infrequently.

practice.question: In the sentence 'The runner sprinted fast to catch the train', what is 'fast'?
practice.explanation: Here, 'fast' is an adverb because it modifies the verb 'sprinted', describing how the runner ran.

practice.question: Identify the adverb of place in: 'He walked downstairs to greet the early guests.'
practice.explanation: 'Downstairs' describes *where* he walked, which makes it an adverb of place.

practice.question: Identify the adverb of manner in: 'The children played happily in the garden all afternoon.'
practice.explanation: 'Happily' describes the cheerful manner in which the children played.

practice.question: Choose the adverb of time in: 'We will soon start our next grammar lesson.'
practice.explanation: 'Soon' is an adverb of time because it answers the question of *when* the action will start.

practice.question: Which word is an adverb of place? 'The puppy ran indoors when the rain started.'
practice.explanation: 'Indoors' is an adverb of place because it describes where the puppy ran.

practice.question: Find the adverb of frequency in: 'They rarely go out for dinner during weekdays.'
practice.explanation: 'Rarely' is an adverb of frequency because it shows how often they go out.

practice.question: Identify the adverb of degree modifying the adjective 'expensive' in: 'The new laptop was rather expensive.'
practice.explanation: 'Rather' modifies the adjective 'expensive', indicating the degree or level of cost.

practice.question: Select the adverb in: 'The students listened attentively to the instructions.'
practice.explanation: 'Attentively' is an adverb of manner because it describes how the students listened.

adjectives.title: Adjectives
adjectives.definition: An adjective is a describing word that modifies or qualifies a noun or pronoun by explaining its traits, size, quantity, or properties.
adjectives.purpose: Adjectives enrich our descriptions, enabling us to differentiate and paint vivid mental pictures for listeners.

examples.text: They live in a gorgeous, modern house down the avenue.
examples.description: Expresses a subjective opinion and descriptive quality.

examples.text: We bought several sweet apples for the pastry.
examples.description: Shows an indefinite quantity of items.

examples.text: That vintage motorcycle belongs to my grandfather.
examples.description: Points directly to a specific singular noun 'motorcycle' further away.

examples.text: Our team celebrated the victory with a grand banquet.
examples.description: Attaches to the noun 'team' to demonstrate ownership.

examples.text: The library contains three ancient leather scrolls.
examples.description: Describes the age and majestic quality of the scrolls.

examples.text: The chef prepared a delicious meal of fresh seafood.
examples.description: Expresses an opinion of taste and quality modifying 'meal'.

examples.text: There are only a few cookies left in the cookie jar.
examples.description: Denotes a small, indefinite quantity of cookies.

examples.text: Those mountains in the distance are covered in snow.
examples.description: Points directly to remote plural nouns ('mountains').

examples.text: My older brother is studying computer engineering in Seattle.
examples.description: Sits in front of the noun 'brother' to indicate who owns the connection.

examples.text: A golden ray of light shone through the glass window.
examples.description: Describes the color and beautiful quality of the light ray.

practice.question: Identify the descriptive adjective in: 'We walked across the sandy beach under the warm sun.'
practice.explanation: 'Sandy' is a descriptive adjective modifying the noun 'beach' to describe its texture. 'Warm' is also one, but sandy is the option provided.

practice.question: What is the role of 'your' in: 'Please wash your hands before dinner.'?
practice.explanation: 'Your' sits directly before the noun 'hands' and describes whose hands they are, making it a possessive adjective.

practice.question: Identify the demonstrative adjective: 'This old grandfather clock still works perfectly.'
practice.explanation: 'This' is a demonstrative adjective modifying 'grandfather clock' and pointing to its close proximity. ('Perfectly' is an adverb).

practice.question: Fill in the blank with a descriptive adjective: 'The _____ puppy kept barking at the mirror.'
practice.explanation: 'Tiny' is an adjective that beautifully describes the size of the puppy.

practice.question: Identify the quantitative adjective in: 'We need some fresh ingredients to bake the strawberry cake.'
practice.explanation: 'Some' is a quantitative adjective indicating an indefinite amount of ingredients.

practice.question: Choose the possessive adjective in the sentence: 'His dedication to learning English grammar is inspiring.'
practice.explanation: 'His' is a possessive adjective because it immediately precedes and modifies the noun 'dedication'.

practice.question: Which word is a descriptive adjective? 'The heavy rain soaked the thirsty ground.'
practice.explanation: 'Thirsty' is a descriptive adjective that describes the dry, eager state of the ground.

practice.question: Find the demonstrative adjective in: 'Those vintage cameras are worth a fortune.'
practice.explanation: 'Those' functions as a demonstrative adjective because it directly points to and modifies the noun 'cameras'.

practice.question: Fill in the blank with an adjective: 'The library is a _____ place to study.'
practice.explanation: 'Quiet' is the adjective form that correctly describes the noun 'place'.

practice.question: Which word is an adjective modifying 'sculpture' in: 'They admired the massive marble sculpture.'?
practice.explanation: 'Massive' (and 'marble') are adjectives modifying 'sculpture'. 'Massive' is the selected option here describing the scale.

conjunctions.title: Conjunctions
conjunctions.definition: A conjunction is a connector word used to link individual words, phrases, independent clauses, or sentences together.
conjunctions.purpose: Conjunctions establish logical relationships (contrast, cause/effect, addition) and bind separate ideas into cohesive thoughts.

examples.text: I bought a fresh sandwich and an organic juice bottle.
examples.description: Connects two items of equal importance (addition).

examples.text: She stayed indoors because it was pouring with rain.
examples.description: Introduces a dependent clause showing the cause or reason.

examples.text: He is extremely talented, yet he remains incredibly humble.
examples.description: Connects two contrasting statements of equal weight.

examples.text: Either you must study hard or you will fail the test.
examples.description: Works in pairs to join alternatives or choices.

examples.text: Although she felt exhausted, she completed the half marathon.
examples.description: Introduces a concession or contrast at the beginning of the sentence.

examples.text: It was getting extremely dark, so we decided to head back home.
examples.description: Connects an action to its logical result/consequence.

examples.text: I listened to study music while completing my chemistry assignments.
examples.description: Denotes that two actions are happening simultaneously.

examples.text: Since you are already here, you can help me prepare the classroom.
examples.description: Introduces a logical reason or premise for the main action.

examples.text: He is quiet but extremely intelligent and helpful.
examples.description: Connects two descriptive qualities with a contrasting relationship.

examples.text: She is not only a brilliant coder but also a talented pianist.
examples.description: Dual connectors working in tandem to link two parallel positive points.

practice.question: Identify the subordinating conjunction in: 'We will go hiking tomorrow unless it rains.'
practice.explanation: 'Unless' is a subordinating conjunction introducing the conditional condition that would stop them from going.

practice.question: Choose the correct coordinating conjunction (contrast): 'He wanted to go to the beach, _____ it was too cold.'
practice.explanation: 'But' is a coordinating conjunction used to show contrast or opposition between two independent ideas.

practice.question: Which conjunction fits perfectly to express cause/effect: 'She took a taxi _____ she was running late.'
practice.explanation: 'Because' is the subordinating conjunction used to introduce the reason why she took a taxi.

practice.question: Fill in the blank: 'Neither Sarah _____ Michael attended the meeting.'
practice.explanation: The correlative pair is 'Neither...nor'. Therefore, 'nor' is the correct conjunction to pair with 'Neither'.

practice.question: Identify the coordinating conjunction expressing result/consequence in: 'The weather forecast predicted a heavy storm, so we cancelled our picnic.'
practice.explanation: 'So' is the coordinating conjunction used to connect a cause to a consequence or result.

practice.question: Choose the correct subordinating conjunction (time): 'I will call you _____ I arrive at the train station.'
practice.explanation: 'As soon as' is a subordinating conjunction of time expressing immediate sequence.

practice.question: Which word is a subordinating conjunction in: 'He didn't eat lunch although he was very hungry.'?
practice.explanation: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction indicating contrast or concession.

practice.question: Select the correlative conjunction pair component: 'Both my sister _____ my mother love reading classic literature.'
practice.explanation: The correlative conjunction pair is 'Both...and'.

practice.question: Find the conjunction in: 'Since we have extra time, let's review the grammar rules once more.'
practice.explanation: 'Since' functions here as a subordinating conjunction introducing the reason why they should review.

practice.question: Fill in the blank: 'We can go to the library now, _____ we can wait until tomorrow morning.'
practice.explanation: 'Or' is a coordinating conjunction offering two alternate, equivalent choices.

interjections.title: Interjections
interjections.definition: An interjection is a word or short exclamation phrase that expresses sudden, strong human emotion, feeling, or surprise. It has no grammatical link to the rest of the sentence.
interjections.purpose: Interjections add emotional color, urgency, and expressiveness to spoken conversational English.

examples.text: Wow! That sunset over the ocean is breathtaking.
examples.description: Used to show amazement or sudden wonder.

examples.text: Ouch! I accidentally hit my toe against the table leg.
examples.description: A sudden phonetic exclamation for physical pain.

examples.text: Oops! I accidentally deleted the entire spreadsheet column.
examples.description: Used when making a minor error or spill.

examples.text: Hooray! Our team won the regional championship trophy.
examples.description: Used to shout out and share absolute happiness.

examples.text: Alas! The beautiful historical cathedral was burned down.
examples.description: A formal or literary expression of deep regret or sorrow.

examples.text: Oh! I understand the entire grammar rule now.
examples.description: Used when suddenly grasping a concept or receiving news.

examples.text: Shh! The librarian asked us to study quietly.
examples.description: Used to demand quietness or reduce ambient volume.

examples.text: Bravo! You gave a perfect presentation on public speaking.
examples.description: Used to applaud great accomplishments or performances.

examples.text: Aha! I finally found where the lost keys were hidden.
examples.description: An exclamation uttered when finding something or solving a problem.

examples.text: Eww! The milk has gone sour and smells awful.
examples.description: Used to show strong dislike, distaste, or disgust.

practice.question: Which interjection is typically used to express sudden pain?
practice.explanation: 'Ouch!' is the standard, universal English exclamation for sudden physical pain.

practice.question: Identify the interjection in: 'Whew, that was a very close call! We almost got in an accident.'
practice.explanation: 'Whew' is an interjection representing a vocal sigh of absolute relief or exhaustion.

practice.question: Choose the interjection expressing excitement/joy to complete the sentence: '_____! We have a week of school holidays!'
practice.explanation: 'Yay' is an interjection used to express immediate excitement, delight, or celebration.

practice.question: What emotion does the interjection 'Ugh' typically express?
practice.explanation: 'Ugh' is commonly uttered to show annoyance, frustration, dislike, or mild disgust.

practice.question: Which interjection is commonly used to request silence?
practice.explanation: 'Shh!' is the standard exclamation used to tell someone to be quiet.

practice.question: Identify the interjection in: 'Aha, I knew I would solve this English crossword puzzle!'
practice.explanation: 'Aha' is an interjection expressing triumph, discovery, or sudden understanding.

practice.question: Choose the interjection expressing praise/approval: '_____! That was an absolutely brilliant performance on stage!'
practice.explanation: 'Bravo' is a loan word used as an interjection to celebrate high excellence or success.

practice.question: What does the interjection 'Oops' typically represent?
practice.explanation: 'Oops' is used to acknowledge small, harmless accidents or slips.

practice.question: Find the interjection in: 'Oh, I didn't realize you were waiting for me here.'
practice.explanation: 'Oh' is an interjection representing sudden realization or minor surprise.

practice.question: Which interjection best expresses mild annoyance or disgust?
practice.explanation: 'Eww' is used specifically to express aversion or disgust towards something unpleasant.

sentences.meaning: Reading instructions precedes starting the activity.

sentences.sentence: I like to stretch before running.
sentences.meaning: Stretching occurs prior to running.

sentences.sentence: Prepare everything before the guests arrive.
sentences.meaning: Preparation must be finished earlier than the arrival.

sentences.sentence: The sky gets dark before it rains.
sentences.meaning: The darkening of the sky precedes the rain.

prepositionsData.title: After
prepositionsData.description: Tell about what occurs later or thereafter
prepositionsData.example: We went for a walk after dinner.
prepositionsData.longDescription: After: Understand how to tell about what occurs later or thereafter. We use "after" when an action follows another event, time, or action.

sentences.sentence: I take a shower after exercising.
sentences.meaning: The shower follows the exercise.

sentences.sentence: She called me after arriving at the office.
sentences.meaning: The call happened following her arrival.

sentences.sentence: We will have dessert after the main course.
sentences.meaning: Dessert follows the main course.

sentences.sentence: The crops grow after the rain stops.
sentences.meaning: Growth happens following the rainfall.

sentences.sentence: He cleaned the kitchen after cooking.
sentences.meaning: Cleaning occurred following cooking.

sentences.sentence: They relaxed after finishing the project.
sentences.meaning: Relaxation follows completion of the work.

sentences.sentence: The sun shines bright after the storm.
sentences.meaning: Brightness follows the storm.

sentences.sentence: We lock the doors after going inside.
sentences.meaning: Locking happens following entry.

prepositionsData.title: During
prepositionsData.description: Throughout the duration of an event
prepositionsData.example: He fell asleep during the movie.
prepositionsData.longDescription: During: State a duration or event when an action takes place inside it. We use "during" when something happens within the time span of an event.

sentences.sentence: Please keep quiet during the presentation.
sentences.meaning: Quietness is required within the presentation span.

sentences.sentence: It rained heavily during the night.
sentences.meaning: Rain occurred within the span of the night.

sentences.sentence: We stayed indoors during the storm.
sentences.meaning: Being indoors lasted throughout the storm.

sentences.sentence: She took notes during the lecture.
sentences.meaning: Note-taking occurred within the lecture time.

sentences.sentence: The baby slept soundly during the flight.
sentences.meaning: Sleep occurred within the span of the flight.

sentences.sentence: Do not use your phone during the exam.
sentences.meaning: Using phones is forbidden within the exam duration.

sentences.sentence: They met many people during their vacation.
sentences.meaning: Meeting people occurred within their vacation span.

sentences.sentence: Birds migration happens during autumn.
sentences.meaning: Migration happens within the autumn season.

prepositionsData.title: While
prepositionsData.description: Express that two things are occurring together
prepositionsData.example: She listened to music while studying.
prepositionsData.longDescription: While: Find out how to express that two things are occurring together. We use "while" to show that two continuous actions are happening simultaneously.

sentences.sentence: I cook dinner while my husband sets the table.
sentences.meaning: Cooking and setting the table happen together.

sentences.sentence: They sang while walking home.
sentences.meaning: Singing and walking home happened at the same time.

sentences.sentence: Keep driving while I look at the map.
sentences.meaning: Driving and looking at the map occur simultaneously.

sentences.sentence: He called me while I was sleeping.
sentences.meaning: The call happened at the same time I was asleep.

sentences.sentence: The dog barked while we were eating.
sentences.meaning: The barking occurred together with our eating.

sentences.sentence: I read a book while waiting for the train.
sentences.meaning: Reading occurs during the simultaneous waiting time.

sentences.sentence: She was smiling while telling the story.
sentences.meaning: Smiling and telling the story occurred together.

sentences.sentence: The phone rang while he was taking a bath.
sentences.meaning: The ringing occurred simultaneously with the bath.

prepositionsData.title: Until
prepositionsData.description: Report the end of a duration
prepositionsData.example: We waited until the rain stopped.
prepositionsData.longDescription: Until: Practice how to report the end of a duration. We use "until" to indicate the exact point in time when an action or state stops.

sentences.sentence: She will stay at home until Monday.
sentences.meaning: Her staying at home stops on Monday.

sentences.sentence: I read the book until I fell asleep.
sentences.meaning: The reading ended at the moment of falling asleep.

sentences.sentence: The shop is open until 10 PM.
sentences.meaning: The opening duration ends at 10 PM.

sentences.sentence: We played games until the lights went out.
sentences.meaning: Playing ended when the lights went out.

sentences.sentence: Keep stirring until the sauce thickens.
sentences.meaning: Stirring stops when the thickening happens.

sentences.sentence: He slept until the sun came up.
sentences.meaning: His sleeping ended at sunrise.

sentences.sentence: Don't open the door until I tell you.
sentences.meaning: The closed state remains up to the command.

sentences.sentence: We walked until we reached the river.
sentences.meaning: Walking stopped when we reached the river.

prepositionsData.title: When
prepositionsData.description: State a duration when something takes place
prepositionsData.longDescription: When: Learn to state a duration or specific moment when something takes place. It links actions directly to their time frame or trigger moment.

sentences.sentence: I was happy when I saw my friend.
sentences.meaning: Happiness occurred at the moment of seeing the friend.

sentences.sentence: He turns off the lights when he leaves.
sentences.meaning: Turning off lights is triggered by leaving.

sentences.sentence: We go indoors when it gets cold.
sentences.meaning: Going indoors happens at the moment of cold temperature.

sentences.sentence: She smiled when she heard the news.
sentences.meaning: Smiling was triggered by hearing the news.

sentences.sentence: The birds fly away when they are scared.
sentences.meaning: Flight is triggered by being scared.

sentences.sentence: I will explain everything when we meet.
sentences.meaning: Explanation happens at the meeting moment.

sentences.sentence: He was five when he learned to swim.
sentences.meaning: Learning to swim occurred at the age of five.

sentences.sentence: The game starts when the whistle blows.
sentences.meaning: Start of game is triggered by the whistle blow.

prepositionsData.title: As
prepositionsData.description: Express that two things are occurring together
prepositionsData.example: He smiled as he waved goodbye.
prepositionsData.longDescription: As: Find out how to express that two things are occurring together. We use "as" to highlight simultaneous actions, often shifting or progressing together.

sentences.sentence: She slipped as she got off the bus.
sentences.meaning: Slipping and getting off the bus occurred together.

sentences.sentence: I saw him as I was leaving.
sentences.meaning: Seeing him occurred simultaneously with my departure.

sentences.sentence: As the sun set, the stars appeared.
sentences.meaning: Star appearance occurred as the sun set.

sentences.sentence: They sang as they walked along.
sentences.meaning: Singing and walking along happened together.

sentences.sentence: He grew wiser as he became older.
sentences.meaning: Growing wise and growing old progress together.

sentences.sentence: She arrived just as we were starting.
sentences.meaning: Her arrival occurred at the exact instant of our start.

sentences.sentence: My heart raced as I opened the envelope.
sentences.meaning: Heart racing occurred together with opening.

sentences.sentence: We watched as the balloon soared up.
sentences.meaning: Watching occurred together with the balloon soaring.

prepositionsData.title: Over
prepositionsData.description: Directly above and covering another object
prepositionsData.example: The plane is flying over the city.
prepositionsData.longDescription: Use "over" when an object is directly above another (often crossing from side to side) or covering the object beneath it completely.

sentences.sentence: The plane is flying over the city.
sentences.meaning: The plane is flying directly above and moving across the city.

sentences.sentence: She hung a warm blanket over the sleeping child.
sentences.meaning: The blanket is covering the child completely.

sentences.sentence: The dog jumped over the wooden fence.
sentences.meaning: The dog leaped across and above the fence from one side to the other.

sentences.sentence: He held an umbrella over her head.
sentences.meaning: The umbrella is positioned above her head to cover/protect her.

sentences.sentence: A beautiful bridge extends over the wide river.
sentences.meaning: The bridge crosses above and covers the width of the river.

sentences.sentence: The clouds are hovering over the mountain.
sentences.meaning: The clouds are directly above and partially covering the mountain peak.

sentences.sentence: He poured syrup over his pancakes.
sentences.meaning: He poured syrup so that it covered the surface of the pancakes.

sentences.sentence: The sign hung over the shop door.
sentences.meaning: The sign was placed directly above the door frame.

prepositionsData.title: Above
prepositionsData.description: Situated higher than another object (not on top)
prepositionsData.example: The picture hangs above the fireplace.
prepositionsData.longDescription: Use "above" when an object is higher than another object but is not touching or covering it directly. It implies a gap between the two objects.

sentences.sentence: The picture hangs above the fireplace.
sentences.meaning: The picture is situated higher than the fireplace, not touching it.

sentences.sentence: The sun rose above the mountain tops.
sentences.meaning: The sun is higher in position than the mountain tops.

sentences.sentence: The shelf is placed above the study desk.
sentences.meaning: The shelf is mounted higher than the desk, leaving a gap.

sentences.sentence: Her apartment is directly above mine.
sentences.meaning: Her flat is located on a higher floor than mine.

sentences.sentence: Keep your head above the water.
sentences.meaning: Maintain your head in a position higher than the water level.

sentences.sentence: The stars shone brightly above us.
sentences.meaning: The stars are high up in the sky overhead.

sentences.sentence: The bird hovered above the tree.
sentences.meaning: The bird remained in the air higher than the tree's branches.

sentences.sentence: We are flying high above the thick clouds.
sentences.meaning: Our position is higher than the clouds below.
